newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria wheat yield 3.21 tonnes/ha, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria wheat yield 3.21 tonnes/ha, seen falling.

text.p: Bulgaria has harvested just over half its wheat area so far, producing an average yield of 3.21 tonnes per hectare, but analysts forecast the final yield will be lower.

"We have collected a total of 2.157 million tonnes of wheat from 671,651 hectares harvested so far and the average yield is 3.21 tonnes per hectare," an agriculture ministry spokeswoman told reporters on Tuesday.
She said 54.8 percent of the sown area had been harvested.

At this level Bulgaria may collect around 3.9 million tonnes of wheat from 1.23 million hectares sown, but analysts see average yield falling because of a delayed harvest, a lack of fertiliser and bad weather.

"Lack of farm machinery delayed the harvest and Bulgaria is obviously missing the ultimate harvest deadline, which is end-July," state Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS) executive director Svetla Bachvarova told Reuters.
This month the cabinet suspended customs duties on imported harvesting machinery until end-1997 in a bid to upgrade its 6,600 outdated combines and help collect the crop.

"Summer rainfalls affected the wheat quality in Bulgaria's northeast major production regions, and cash-strapped producers could not afford to treat the crop with fertiliser and plant protection sprays," Bachvarova said.
However, the Balkan state has not suffered the very heavy rainfall seen in eastern Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic.
AMIS forecasts an average wheat yield of 2.80 tonnes per hectare.
The agriculture ministry declined to make preliminary forecasts, saying that much depended on the weather.
In May Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov estimated this year's wheat crop at around 2.4 million tonnes and forecasts were based on an assumed average yield of two tonnes per hectare.
Varbanov said Bulgaria needed 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat to cover a consumption gap before the 1998 crop.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under contracts agreed earlier this year. Poland has said it could accept cash payment for 100,000 of the total.
Bulgaria's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.

"Producers are reluctant to sell their wheat, hoping for better prices in September following the rise of dollar denominated international prices and the fall of the mark against the dollar," Bachvarova said.
"The only deals struck so far are to settle forward contracts or to cover payments on bank credits," she added.

The minimum purchase price is set at 230 marks per tonne from this year's crop in a bid to secure the country's grain balance after excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 caused acute grain shortages earlier this year.
An export fee of 15 percent of international wheat prices has been also set in a bid to curb exports.
